reason: Correct population random-assignment identification and final ATT-plus-selection-bias identity, with measurable integrable outcomes and positive arms. The canonical claim additionally contains the sample difference-in-means plug-in formula and two intermediate equalities, which are absent. The binary fair-treatment/constant-potential-outcome instance in nonvacuity.md satisfies all premises.

Includes the countable-covariate ATE sum, general-covariate conditional ATE, balance conditional on the propensity score, potential-outcome independence conditional on the score, and positivity given the score. The score result is quantified independently without outcome moments. CEF and conditional independence are standard integral/indicator formulations; overlap and integrability make the displayed sums and expectations legitimate. Versions on null sets are read as authorized in the standing assumptions. A singleton covariate and fair treatment with constant outcomes give a joint instance.

Both the IPW formula and the two double-robustness alternatives are correct. The separately imposed integrability of each nuisance regression excludes cases where only the combined augmented score is integrable. For fair treatment, zero outcomes, p=q=1/2 and m1=N,m0=-N with nonintegrable positive N independent of treatment, the combined score is identically zero. This is a genuine narrowing, beyond requiring the displayed expectation to exist. Overlap otherwise controls denominators and all expectations in the stated domain are integrable. Concrete instances of both alternatives are in nonvacuity.md.

The theorem asserts the negation of each of the two printed universal assertions. Both are valid refutations of their printed readings: the constant functional has zero derivative and identically zero plug-in fluctuations, so no positive-variance Gaussian limit; finite-second-moment remote contamination approaches a baseline CDF at order t^2 but changes its mean by one, contradicting sup-norm Hadamard differentiability along direction zero. The latter works even at a nondegenerate Bernoulli baseline. The bounded-function space and CDF domain match the stated Kolmogorov topology; no unbounded supremum or nonintegrable mean is involved.

Negates the fixed-covariate consistency reading rather than asserting the printed positive result. This refutation is legitimate: with equally probable binary X, true success probabilities 1/4 and 3/4, and a covariate-independent Bernoulli model t in [1/4,3/4], the fixed x=0 conditional KL has unique minimizer 1/4 but the actual-product MLE tends to 1/2. The fixed covariate has probability 1/2, all observed probabilities are positive and all logs/KL integrands finite. Thus the negation does not exploit a null conditioning event or an undefined likelihood.

States a concrete negation of full-vector MLE consistency in a legitimate two-component mixture. With p=1, the second component's parameter b does not affect the data law. The count-based product maximizer can choose b=1/4 whenever the inactive cells are absent, including almost surely under true b0=3/4, so the vector cannot converge to the claimed true vector. The maximizer can be defined on every sample, and the parameter constraints are nonempty. Failure of consistency refutes the printed consistency-and-efficiency conjunction without needing an efficiency assertion.

Asserts an existential counterexample to the printed size claim, at alpha=1/2. A finite-cell IID law with X uniform on {-1,0,1}, independent fair Z, D conditionally Bernoulli(1/4+X^2/2), and W=X^2+Z/2 has W independent of D given X. Its restricted/full Gram determinants are 2/3 and 17/54, full risk 59/272, and F_n/n tends to 64/531>0. Actual F(1,n-3) medians stay bounded. The guarded rejection probability therefore tends to one, while the good-design event holds eventually almost surely. Rejections cannot rely on a singular inverse, zero residual risk, zero degrees of freedom or a fabricated critical value. See nonvacuity.md and scratch/Check.lean.

The finite-second-moment IID WLLN is the finite-variance claim under the standing finite-expectation convention, including the printed zero-variance footnote. The sample mean and convergence-in-probability definitions agree with the printed ones, up to the harmless initial n=0 term. IID standard Gaussians and a deterministic constant sequence exhibit positive- and zero-variance instances.

Both printed CLT forms and the finite standardization identity and standardized moments are present. MemLp 2 and positive real variance give exactly finite positive variance with legitimate expectations. The finite identities are restricted to positive sample sizes, avoiding a zero standardization denominator. IID standard Gaussians satisfy all premises.

The displayed rectangle kernel and 1/(n h_n) normalization are exact. Positive deterministic bandwidths, h_n tending to zero, n h_n tending to infinity and a globally continuous PDF reproduce the canonical statement read with the preceding sentence. The conclusion is for each fixed x, as printed. Closed endpoints carry zero mass under a PDF, and finite local kernel variances suffice without moments of X. Standard Gaussian data with h_n=1/sqrt(n+1) give an instance.

Asserts existence of the actual open-interval coverage limit and the printed bound at least 1-alpha, using exactly n-scaled variance consistency and positive asymptotic Gaussian variance. Nonnegative variance estimates make the printed real square root meaningful. It does not replace a limit by an unrestricted limsup or assume coverage as a hypothesis. A normal location estimator theta+phi Z/sqrt(n+1) with variance estimate phi^2/(n+1) satisfies every premise and has coverage 1-alpha.

Correct actual-product MLE consistency under explicit compactness, expected-log separation and a finite uniform error envelope converging in probability, together with a separately quantified correct true-model expected-log maximum/equality lemma. The envelope is an additional uniform convergence assumption and is required at every sample size, sample point and parameter; it is not derived from the informal printed regularities. The separate product-log identity, unique sample maximizer and pointwise WLLN conclusion are absent. A Bernoulli family on [1/4,3/4] with an explicit envelope log(3)|sample success fraction-1/2| (and a finite initial value) gives a nontrivial joint instance, so the consistency premise is not the conclusion in disguise.

Both displayed completed-outcome estimators are unbiased at every positive n and consistent for exactly the displayed lower/upper endpoints. Only observable pairs must be IID, as printed. Bounds and almost-sure binary response ensure integrability; positive response-arm probabilities make the conditional mean ratio legitimate. The target is endpoint estimation, not a separate sharpness or population-bound theorem. Constant Y=1/2 with fair IID response and [a,b]=[0,1] yields endpoints 1/4 and 3/4 and satisfies every premise.
